transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello. Nice to meet you too. Well, mostly I'm here because I just don't sleep right anymore. I lie there a long time at night... and then I wake up from bad dreams, or even just little noises. After that, I just can't seem to settle back down.
Have you been through a traumatic event that still affects you?

Yeah, I did. I had a bad accident a ways back, and I guess it still bothers me. Sometimes, if I hear a piece of metal scrape, or... well, even if I just see a ladder leaning up in somebody's yard, the whole thing jumps right back in my head. It feels just like I'm stuck right back under there all over again, just waiting for help to come.
Do you go out of your way to avoid things that remind you of the accident?

Yeah, I guess I do. I just... I keep finding reasons not to go down to the senior center these days. And I don't really work around the garage much anymore, either. I just stay away from it, specially near the tools and that spot where I used to keep that ladder.
Do you feel constantly on guard or easily startled, even when you're safe?

Yeah, I'd say so. It don't take much. If a door bangs shut, or... well, if somebody just walks up behind me, I jump real hard. And even after I turn around and see who it is, and I know it's nothing to worry about, my chest just keeps thumping for a good while. It just takes a bit for my heart to calm back down.
Since the accident, have you felt blame toward yourself or anyone else for what happened?
No, I don't think so. I mean, it was just an accident. I was up on the ladder, and it gave way. I don't blame anybody for it, not even myself. It's just one of those things that happens, you know?
Since the accident, have you been feeling down or hopeless much of the time?
No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I have my days where I'm a bit tired or just... not up to much, but I don't feel hopeless or anything like that. I'm just getting by, taking it one day at a time.
Are the bad dreams about the accident?
No, I don't really have any bad dreams about it. I sleep alright, mostly. Just... no, no nightmares or anything like that.
Do unwanted memories of the accident pop into your mind during the day, even when you don't want them to?

Well, yeah, sometimes they do. Like... if I hear metal scraping, or even just if I'm driving by and see a ladder leaning up against somebody's house. It just sort of jumps right back into my head, clear as day. Almost like I'm right back under there, just... waiting for somebody to come help me. It just pops up when I'm not expecting it.
How long has this been going on since the accident?
Well, it's been going on ever since the ladder accident. That was about a year and seven months ago now.
When something reminds you of the accident, do you get a strong rush of fear?
No, not really a rush of fear. I mean, it's unpleasant, sure, but I don't feel terrified or anything. It's just... a memory that comes back. I don't get all worked up or scared about it.
When those memories come up, does it ever feel like you’re actually back at the accident, as if it’s happening again right then?

No, no it doesn't. I mean... I remember it real clear, but I know I'm not actually back under that ladder. I know I'm just standing on the street or sitting in my truck. It doesn't feel like it's happening all over again right then. It's just... just a picture in my head that I can't help thinking about. I don't lose track of where I'm at or nothing like that.
Outside of thoughts about the accident, do you find yourself worrying a lot about everyday things?
No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things like anybody else, I suppose, but I don't sit around fretting over every little everyday thing. It's just that ladder business that sticks with me.
When you go to bed, do you often have trouble falling asleep even when nothing has reminded you of the accident?

Well, honestly, that's mostly why I'm here. I just don't sleep right anymore. I'll lie there for a long time trying to drift off, and even when I do, I end up waking up from bad dreams or just... little noises in the house. And once I'm awake, I just can't seem to settle back down to get any real rest.
When you wake up from those bad dreams, are the dreams about the ladder accident?

No, they aren't about the accident. That's the funny thing about it. I mean, I'll wake up sweating and my heart will be racing, but the dreams... they're just jumbled up nonsense, mostly. Nothing to do with work or ladders or anything like that. I don't even remember them half the time, just that they were bad enough to wake me up.
When a little noise wakes you at night, do you immediately feel on guard, like something bad might be happening?

Yeah, I suppose I do. I get a bit jumpy, like I'm waiting for something to go wrong. But it ain't just at night in the house, either. 

Even during the day, when I go places now, I... well, I'm just always looking around. I find myself checking up above to see what might fall, or figuring out where the exits are. I even catch myself looking real close at the floor or the steps to make sure they're steady before I can finally sit easy. I just can't seem to let my guard down like I used to.
